POP-1.claim: The per-market derivation covered 72 of the 97 roster markets. The remaining 25 run on class calibration, and 13 of those 25 measure negative beyond two standard errors on the held-back confirm fold while the engine still trades them — losses up to -1.833R per setup, five times worse than the worst market the engine declines.
POP-1.population: 13 markets traded today with a class-inherited cell and a measured negative: ALGOUSD, ARWUSD, AVAXUSD, DOTUSD, DYDXUSD, HEUSX, NEARUSD, THETAUSD, TRUMPUSD, TRXUSD, XTZUSD, ZFUSD, ZRUSD. The wider affected set is the 25 roster markets with no derived cell.
POP-1.whyMissed: Amendment 33 says 'per market, never per class', but the 4d pipeline's own gate structure made 'no cell' an absorbing state: capacity-gated, measure-only, starved and held-out markets were dropped from the candidate set (calibration.ts:688-698 records exactly that), and nothing downstream re-asked whether the class value they fell back to was itself defensible for them. Falling out of the derivation was treated as 'no change', not as 'unmeasured'.
POP-1.remedy: Re-derive per market for all 25 cell-less roster markets on their own spans (the totality-tranche method already exists in scripts/derive-4d.ts), and run each through the amendment-36 published-commission test. Until that lands, the 13 with a measured negative beyond 2 s.e. should enter ENGINE_DECLINED_MARKETS on the numbers already in roster-expectancy-audit.json, or the engine is knowingly trading markets its own corpus says lose.
POP-1.reviewed: HIGH — real, undispositioned, and it changes what ships; but scope is the 25 cell-less markets, not the roster, and the remedy is re-derivation of geometry, not withdrawal

POP-2.claim: The engine's decline register can never contain a market that has no derived cell, because its stated entry condition requires one — so the 97-market roster is gated by a mechanism whose domain is only 72 markets.
POP-2.population: The 25 cell-less roster markets, which are structurally ineligible for withdrawal no matter what they measure.
POP-2.whyMissed: The withdrawal standard was written against the artifact that produced it (4d-cost-sensitivity.json) rather than against the roster. Pinning the register 'in both directions' to that artifact makes it self-consistent and roster-incomplete at the same time — the pin can never fire on a market the artifact never contained.
POP-2.remedy: Restate amendment 36's precondition against the ROSTER, not against the derived-cell set: every roster market gets a confirm-fold expectancy at its shipped settings (whatever their provenance) and a published-commission-only re-run before the register is considered complete. Add a test asserting ENGINE_DECLINED_MARKETS ∪ {measured non-negative} = defaultScanSymbols.

AXES-9.claim: HANDOFF item 8c is unchanged in today's code: the momentum voter still cannot vote sell on mixed oscillator evidence, because the buy branch is evaluated first. It fires on 100% of decision points and its bias has never been measured or costed.
AXES-9.population: All 97 roster markets. The voter is one of eight and appears in the votes array of every corpus record.

Item 4 then ran a full calibration program on top of a decision stream this defect shapes, because the program's scope was geometry and the voter is scoring. The corpus already holds both the votes and realizedR. Fix the precedence only after the cost is known — flipping it changes the decision stream and therefore invalidates the 4c/4d corpus.

AXES-10.claim: Two of the 25 CategoryCalibration fields are dead — set on all eight classes, consumed by nothing. Sixteen values are maintained, commented and pinned as if they were calibration.
AXES-10.population: All 8 classes x 2 fields = 16 maintained values with zero effect on any setup.

E1.claim: Production resolves every setup on 15-minute bars while the entire 4c/4d corpus resolved on 5-minute bars, and the difference in realized expectancy is larger than the whole measured edge of every market in the roster.
E1.population: All 97 roster markets. Every one of the 72 derived cells and all 49 markets the audit calls MEASURABLY POSITIVE — the divergence (-0.21 to -0.28 R) exceeds the measured edge of each of them; the largest edge in the roster is +0.3192.
E1.whyMissed: The resolver's fill options are constructed in two unrelated places — the sweep driver builds them inline (sweep.ts:560-575) and production builds them in fillOptionsFromRiskModel (replay.ts:117-145) — and no test compares the two option objects. The FR-5 change that moved the corpus to 5-minute resolution was made only on the sweep side; tests/sweepDecisionContext.test.ts:417-461 asserts live/replay parity for the daily-completion module and for the 5-min series' 40-bar admission floor, and stops there, so the interval the RESOLVER reads was never in scope of any parity assertion.
E1.remedy: Either resolve production on 5-minute bars (fetch "5min" in outcome-sync and set barIntervalMs accordingly, matching the corpus), or re-derive the whole 4c/4d cube at 15-minute resolution. Do not ship a derived cell until the corpus's resolution interval and outcome-sync's are the same constant, imported from one place, and pinned by a test that reads both call sites.
E1.reviewed: CRITICAL — redo-required, and escalated: the numbers are right, the diagnosis is wrong, and acting on the stated diagnosis would import the artifact into production

E2.claim: The corpus's 5-minute series is roughly 1x, not 3x, the 15-minute row count; roughly 69% of confirm-fold decisions had review windows with no 5-minute bars, and every one of them entered the corpus as a phantom "unfilled" that the expectancy denominator then silently discards.
E2.population: Every market and every fold in sweeps/4c/*.jsonl — the corpus behind all 72 derived cells, the confirm read, and the 97-market roster audit. Measured directly on EURUSD, BTCUSD, XAUUSD; the cache ratio is ~1.0 for all three, so the defect is structural to FMP's 5-min row cap, not market-specific.
E2.whyMissed: evaluateSetupOutcome reports "I had no bars" through the same enum value it uses for "the limit never traded", and the sweep treats any state==="resolved" as a successful measurement (sweep.ts:578-583 only diverts state!=="resolved" into planRejected). Downstream nothing can tell the two apart. The manifest records per-series firstTime/lastTime and row counts (scripts/sweepManifest.ts:162) but no check ever asserted the 5-min count against 3x the 15-min count, so a series with 23-day holes passed provenance as complete.
E2.remedy: Add a distinct resolution state for "no bars in the review window" and refuse to count those decisions at all (neither filled nor unfilled). Assert in assertManifest that each symbol's 5-min row count is >= 2.5x its 15-min count over the swept span, and fail the run otherwise. Then re-sweep; every expectancy in 4d-candidates/4d-confirm-read/roster-expectancy-audit is computed over a coverage-selected subsample until that is done.
E2.reviewed: HIGH — mechanism confirmed exactly, framing corrected: it costs ~2/3 of the corpus and voids every fill-rate figure in the record, but on its own it does not bias expectancy (the bias is E1's clock error)

E3.claim: market.latest comes from a different timeframe in production (the 1-minute series) than in the sweep (the 15-minute decision bar), so the entry-viability gate and the execution-cost anchor read a price the corpus never had — production silently refuses to build plans the corpus counted, and the ones it does build are selected for having drifted AWAY from the limit.
E3.population: Every roster market for which FMP returns >=40 1-minute bars (marketLoader.ts:148 + 414-417) — effectively all 97, and all 72 derived cells. Compounding this: dailyCompletion.ts gates only the daily series (applied at index.ts:709 and sweep.ts:337); no completion gate exists for the 15min/5min/1hour/4hour series, so production's decision bar may also be a forming 15-minute bar while every corpus decision bar is complete.
E3.whyMissed: buildDecisionMarketContext was written to mirror the live loader's availableTimeframes construction order and the 5-min admission floor, and tests/sweepDecisionContext.test.ts:361-364 pins latest/latestTimeframe/quote to the SWEEP's own shape rather than comparing them against pickLatestTimeframe's output. A test that asserts a value equals itself cannot detect a fork. The 2a work closed exactly this defect for the daily series and the identical question was never asked of the intraday series.
E3.remedy: Decide which price is the decision anchor and make both paths use it. Either pin latestTimeframe to the primary timeframe in the live loader (so currentClose === latest.close as the corpus assumed), or feed the sweep a 1-minute tail so the drift and the entry-viability refusals are in the corpus. Then add a parity test that constructs a live-shaped context and a sweep-shaped context from the same bars and asserts buildPricePlan returns the same plan. Until then the corpus over-counts accepted decisions by an unmeasured amount and its filled population is not production's.
E3.reviewed: HIGH — confirmed as an engine-conformance defect, with one correction: the remedy is a fix in the analyzer plus re-verification, NOT a re-derivation of the 72 cells. The corpus geometry is not what is wrong here; the shipped engine does not reproduce it.

E4.claim: Production emits at most one setup per correlation group per scan and also suppresses any candidate whose group already holds a stronger setup from the last six hours; the corpus measured every market independently, so 31 of the 49 measurably-positive markets were derived on a population production will not trade.
E4.population: 31 of the 49 measurably-positive markets, named above; and the conditional expectancy of the 18 that do win is likewise unmeasured, because winning is conditional on confidence, which the whole learning apparatus asserts is predictive.
E4.whyMissed: Correlation collapse lives in the scan orchestration layer of index.ts, not in the shared engine modules the sweep imports (calibration/strategies/pricePlan/replay). Every parity effort so far has been scoped to the shared modules, so a gate that decides WHICH of two qualifying setups reaches the operator was never in the comparison surface at all.
E4.remedy: The corpus already carries confidenceScore and time per decision, so this is a read, not a re-sweep: replay the collapse offline across each correlation group's decisions on a common clock, keep only the winner, and recompute per-market expectancy on the surviving population. Report both the winner-only expectancy and the share of each market's decisions that survive.
E4.reviewed: MODERATE — measure-required, exactly as labeled. I trim one word of the framing: these 31 markets are not 'a population production will not trade'; they are markets production trades only when they win their group, so what is unmeasured is the conditional expectancy, not the existence of the trade.

E5.claim: Production's news gate reads an event table containing two families the corpus has none of — fmp_earnings events that BLOCK the whole review, and fmp_news headline events that add penalty units — and the two paths disagree on currency-less events in opposite directions.
E5.population: 10 equity-index markets for the blocking family (4 of them shipped derived cells); 22 markets for the headline penalty (15 measurably positive); all 97 for the currency-default asymmetry.
E5.whyMissed: The sweep's news join was built against FMP's economic-calendar endpoint directly rather than against the economic_events table the live analyzer queries. Two ingestion vocabularies were never reconciled because the shared module (newsRules.ts) covers only the SCORING of events, not their provenance — so the shared-rules comment at newsRules.ts:1-2 ("so scheduled-event blocking and penalties behave identically in both") is true of the arithmetic and false of the inputs.
E5.remedy: Have the sweep read the same economic_events table production reads, or at minimum add the earnings and headline families and the USD default to the replay join. For the 10 equity-index markets the measured decision population includes decisions production refuses outright, so their cells need re-deriving after the join is fixed.
E5.killed:
KILLED — mechanism real, severity inflated by roughly two orders of magnitude, and two of its three arms measure empty.

ARM 1 (earnings blocking, claimed 'redo-required' for 10 markets incl. 4 derived cells): I read the writer the claim cites. supabase/functions/news-calendar/index.ts:18-28 shows MARKET_MOVING_EARNINGS_SYMBOLS is nine US mega-caps (AAPL AMZN AVGO GOOGL GOOG META MSFT NVDA TSLA). Earnings are quarterly, so this family emits about 36 rows a year. The block window is not a day or a session — trade-analyzer/index.ts:2046-2048 sets activeStart/activeEnd to now-10min..now+20min, and only events inside that window reach `blocking` (index.ts:2069, newsRules.ts:15-17). Total production-only exclusion: ~36 half-hour windows a year on 10 markets, against a corpus of thousands of decision points per market. That cannot move a derived cell's expectancy and is not grounds to re-derive anything.

ARM 2 (currency-default asymmetry, claimed population 'all 97'): measured, not argued. I pulled FMP's economic calendar for 2026-08-03..2026-08-11 (758 events, 137 medium/high) and counted rows with a missing or empty currency: ZERO, and zero among medium/high. replay-sweep.ts:496's `if (Number.isFinite(time) && currency)` therefore drops nothing. The claim also mis-reads its own code path: news-calendar/index.ts:323 and :528 write `String(event.currency ?? "USD")`, so a null currency never reaches the table as null — index.ts:2091-2093's 'null currency is relevant to everything' branch is reachable only for an empty-string currency, which the provider did not produce once in 758 events.

ARM 3 (headline penalty, claimed 22 markets / 15 measurably positive): the penalty enters only through scoreSetupConfidence, and confidence gates acceptance only where confidenceThreshold > 0 (index.ts:1213-1215). All 72 derived cells ship confidenceThreshold: 0 (I counted: 72 occurrences of `confidenceThreshold: 0,` in calibration.ts, against 8 nonzero class values). Intersecting the 22 headline-mapped symbols (symbols.ts:145-168) with the 25 threshold-bearing markets leaves exactly three: ASX, DOW, NIKKEI — none of which holds a derived cell (all read 'class calibration (no derived cell)' in roster-expectancy-audit.json). For the other 19 headline-mapped markets the penalty cannot change acceptance at all; it can only change scan ranking, which is E4's mechanism, not a new one.

What would have made it survive: a measured non-trivial rate of currency-less calendar rows, or an earnings family broad enough to cover a real share of decision points, or headline mappings landing on threshold-bearing derived cells. None of the three holds. The true residue — production's news model is a strict superset of the corpus's — is worth one bounded sensitivity check, not a re-sweep, and it is already dominated by E6.

E6.claim: For the 25 class-gated markets, every measurement applied the live confidence threshold to a score that omits four terms production adds — global learning (+/-10), macro rate (+/-2), provider-warning penalty, and headline-news penalty — so the population behind their verdicts is not the population production admits.
E6.population: The 25 class-gated markets named above, including all 13 the audit already flags as measurably negative and still tradable.
E6.whyMissed: Every derived cell ships confidenceThreshold 0, so on the 72 derived markets these four terms cannot change acceptance and the fork is invisible. The 25 class-gated markets were then folded into the same audit script and read with the same corpus, without re-checking that the script's threshold filter reproduces the score production computes. The version-scoped learning read (index.ts:1160-1176) also means weightAdjustment is 0 today at the freshly-bumped ANALYZER_VERSION (calibration.ts:7, "2026.08.11.declines") and grows away from zero as live outcomes accrue — so the fork widens after ship rather than at ship, which is the worst shape for detection.
E6.remedy: Either give the sweep the three missing inputs (fetch the live macro series into the replay, join the learning table at the swept ANALYZER_VERSION or state that it must be zero, add the headline/provider terms) or set the 25 class thresholds to 0 and gate them the way the derived markets are gated. Separately and immediately: the 13 measurably-negative markets are being traded against the engine's own audit — either decline them or state why the audit does not bind them.
E6.reviewed: MODERATE-TO-HIGH for the 25 class-gated markets — measure-required, not redo-required. Two of the four omitted terms are inert or dormant today; the other two are live, and the population most exposed is exactly the 13 markets the audit calls measurably negative and still tradable.

E7.claim: Production prefers the provider's quoted bid/ask spread over the modeled one for both the payoff gate and the live resolver's fill prices; the corpus never had a quote at all, so no cost number behind any derived cell has ever been checked against the spread production will actually charge.
E7.population: Every roster market for which FMP's /quote returns a usable bid and ask (quotes.ts:15-19) — unenumerated. All 72 derived cells are exposed through the payoff gate and through the resolver's halfSpread.
E7.whyMissed: quote: null is a documented, deliberate property of the offline context and the quoted branch is unit-tested in isolation, so both halves looked correct. Nobody asked the joint question — what fraction of live reviews take the quoted branch, and by how much does it move estimatedSpread against the modeled number every derived cell was fitted on. The corpus's provenance manifest records bar series but not quotes, so the absence leaves no trace.
E7.remedy: Instrument the live analyzer to record spreadSource and quotedSpread/modeledSpread per review (executionQuality already returns both, executionQuality.ts:293-297), run a week of scans, and publish the per-class ratio. If the quoted branch is taken materially often and diverges, either bank quotes into the replay corpus or stop preferring them until the corpus can price them.
E7.killed:
KILLED — the population is empty, measured directly against the provider.

The code reading is correct: executionQuality.ts:203-207 makes a quoted spread outrank the entire modeled branch (`estimatedSpread = quotedSpread === null ? modeledSpread : max(quotedSpread, COST_EPSILON)` — not a max against the model), sweep.ts:270 sets `quote: null` and tests/sweepDecisionContext.test.ts:364 pins it, and replay.ts:128-142 re-reads the persisted estimatedSpread as the resolver's halfSpread. But the claim never enumerated its own population ('unenumerated'), and that omission is the whole claim.

quotes.ts parseFmpQuoteSnapshot returns null unless the payload carries BOTH a positive bid and a positive ask with ask > bid. I queried FMP's live /quote (the same stable endpoint marketLoader.ts:127-130 fetches) for 14 roster symbols spanning every asset class the roster contains — EURUSD, XAUUSD (FOREX); BTCUSD, ETHUSD, XRPUSD, SOLUSD (CRYPTO); GCUSD, ESUSD, CLUSD, ZNUSD, ZCUSX (COMMODITY); ^NDX, ^N225, ^AXJO (INDEX) — via both the batch and single-symbol forms. Not one response contains a `bid` or `ask` field. The fields are absent from the schema for these exchanges, not merely null at this hour, so this is not a liquidity-of-the-moment artifact.

Consequence: spreadSource is 'modeled' on every roster review, the payoff gate charges the same modeled spread the corpus charged, and the resolver's halfSpread is that same modeled number. 'No cost number behind any derived cell has ever been checked against the spread production will actually charge' is false — production charges the modeled spread, which is exactly what was measured.

What would have made it survive: any roster symbol whose /quote returns a usable bid/ask. What remains is a latent robustness note (if FMP ever adds bid/ask for FX/crypto/commodities, a live branch no corpus ever exercised switches on silently, for every market at once) — worth a guard or a telemetry counter, not weeks of re-sweeping.
